full_text_zh:
[P1] 腊八节的故事
连环画出版社

[P2] 腊八节的故事
司南/改编
方骏/绘画
连环画出版社

[P3] 农历十二月又叫腊月。腊月初八是腊八节，这一天，人们都要喝腊八粥。

熬腊八粥要用各种米和豆子：像白米、黄米、江米啦，红豆、绿豆、芸豆啦……还可以加入喜欢的果子，如大枣、花生和杏仁等，熬啊，熬啊，熬成一锅香喷喷的腊八粥，让你喝了一碗还想喝。

[P4] 喝着香喷喷的腊八粥，老爷爷讲起了“瞌睡虫”和“没底锅”的故事。
从前啊，有这么一家三口：爸爸、妈妈和儿子。

[P5] 爸爸最勤劳。他每天鸡叫就起床，天刚亮就下地干活儿。他说：“手是摇钱树，铺成金光路。”
妈妈最节俭，过日子精打细算，她补的衣服又密又好。她说：“天下哪有聚宝盆，勤俭才成富裕人。”

[P6] 他们家呀，米面满仓，
鸡鸭成群，瓜果成架。
但他家有个懒儿子。这个儿子整天
吃饱了就睡，邻居叫他“瞌睡虫”。

[P7] 老两口年纪大了。爸爸对儿子说：“要吃饭，得流汗。你得学着种庄稼，光睡觉可不行啊！”
妈妈对儿子说：“爹娘不能跟你一辈子，你不会过日子，老了可怎么办呀？”

[P8] 这种人，好姑娘谁愿意嫁呀？结果“瞌睡虫”娶了个媳妇儿，和他一样懒。
她太阳没落就睡，日上三竿不起，油瓶倒了都不扶。邻居都叫她“没底锅”。

[P9] 过了几年，老两口得了重病。他们不放心地嘱咐“瞌睡虫”和“没底锅”：“要想日子过得好，勤劳节俭不能少。饭要及时衣要暖，地要深耕细锄草。”不久，老两口就先后去世了。
“瞌睡虫”觉得老两口不会享福。他对媳妇儿说：“粮满仓，豆满仓，何必犯傻种地忙？”

[P10] “没底锅”觉得日子过得挺好，不用发愁。她对丈夫说：“有单衣，有棉被，织布不如把觉睡。”
两个人谁也没把老人的话放在心上，每天除了吃喝玩乐，还是吃喝玩乐。坐吃山空呀，没几年，地荒了，家里也没存粮了。

[P11] 这年腊月初八，北风“呼呼”地刮，雪花飘呀飘，简直有巴掌那么大。
“瞌睡虫”和“没底锅”没吃没穿，缩在破房子里直打哆嗦。
“哆嗦嗦，哆嗦嗦，好想妈蒸的白馍馍。”“哎哟哟，哎哟哟，扫把杂粮凑碗粥。”杂粮是从缸底、粮仓缝、墙边、老鼠洞……好不容易找出来的。谁知他们端起碗刚想喝，一阵大风刮来，房子“呼啦”一下塌了。

[P12] 根据这个传说，每年的
腊八，家家都要熬上一锅杂
粮粥，喝粥过节，用来提醒
自己，珍惜好生活。

老话说“报信儿的腊八粥”。腊八粥是腊八
节这一天最重要的食物。你可别小看这道粥，怎
么做，做什么，可都是有讲究的。

明朝时，皇上吃的腊八粥是这么做的：在
腊八前几天，把红枣捶破以后泡汤，到腊八当天
早上，加入粳米、白果、核桃仁、栗子、菱米煮
粥。老百姓虽然没这么讲究，但是一样要放很多
东西，清代的老百姓用黄米、白米、江米、小
米、菱角米、栗子、红江豆、去皮的枣泥等等，
一块放在水里煮熟了，再将染红的桃仁、杏仁、
瓜子、花生、榛子、松子以及白糖、红糖、葡萄
什么的一块放进去，这样又好看又好吃。

这些东西都是有说头的，桂圆象征富贵团
圆，百合象征百事和睦，红枣花生比喻早生贵
子，莲子心象征恩爱连心，核桃表示合合美美，
橘脯、栗子象征大吉大利等等。大家盼着以后生
活能更加美好。

[P13] 除了腊八粥，北方民间到了腊八，也会泡腊八蒜。腊八泡蒜，大年享用。腊八蒜的做法特别简单：在腊八这一天，把剥了皮的蒜瓣儿放到一个装满醋的坛子里，封口，然后放到一个冷一点儿的地方。蒜被醋泡过以后，辣味淡了很多，吃起来也变得又嫩又脆，而泡过蒜的醋则有了蒜香，这种醋叫“腊八醋”。泡在醋里的蒜不但味道会变，连颜色也变了，会越变越绿，泡得好的，最后整个蒜都是碧绿碧绿的，跟翡翠一样好看。腊八蒜有没有做成功，主要也是看是不是变绿。这种蒜啊，吃起来可以防寒，还可以预防感冒呢。
当然啦，腊八蒜主要是为了除夕晚上的饺子准备的。腊八泡上，年三十正好能吃。现在有暖气，不用几天腊八蒜就能做得，晚几天也能泡好，即使这样，泡出来的也叫腊八蒜。除夕晚上就着热腾腾、香喷喷的饺子，咬上一口腊八蒜，那味道，真没得说！

full_text_en:
[P1] The Story of Laba Festival
Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P2] The Story of Laba Festival
Si Nan / Adapted
Fang Jun / Illustrated
Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P3] The twelfth month of the lunar calendar is also called the 12th lunar month. The 8th day of this month is Laba Festival, and on this day, people all drink Laba porridge.

To make Laba porridge, you need various kinds of rice and beans: like white rice, yellow rice, glutinous rice, red beans, mung beans, and adzuki beans... you can also add your favorite fruits, such as red dates, peanuts, and almond kernels. Boil, boil, boil until you have a pot of delicious Laba porridge that makes you want to have another bowl after finishing the first.

[P4] Sipping the fragrant Laba porridge, Grandpa began telling the story of the 'sleepy bug' and the 'bottomless pot'.
Long ago, there was a family of three: father, mother, and son.

[P5] Dad is the hardest worker. He gets up at the crow of the rooster and goes to work in the fields as soon as it's light. He says, 'Hands are money trees, paving the golden road.'
Mom is the most thrifty, managing the household carefully and precisely. The clothes she mends are both tight and well-made. She says, 'There's no such thing as a treasure basin in the world; only thrift and diligence make a wealthy person.'

[P6] Their home had full granaries of rice and flour,
with flocks of chickens and ducks, and racks full of melons and fruits.
But he had a lazy son. This son slept all day after eating,
and neighbors called him "Sleepyhead."

[P7] The old couple was getting old. Dad said to his son, "To eat, you must sweat. You must learn to grow crops; just sleeping won't work!"
Mom said to her son, "We can't be with you forever. If you don't know how to manage life, what will you do when you get old?"

[P8] People like this—what good girl would want to marry him? In the end, the 'sleepyhead' married a wife who was just as lazy.
She went to sleep before the sun set, didn't get up until after the sun had risen high, and didn't even bother to pick up a spilled oil bottle. Neighbors called her 'bottomless pot'.

[P9] After a few years, the old couple fell seriously ill. They worriedly advised 'Sleepyhead' and 'Bottomless Pot': 'If you want to live a good life, diligence and frugality are essential. Food must be timely, clothes must be warm, and fields must be deeply tilled and carefully weeded.' Soon after, the old couple passed away one after another.
'Sleepyhead' thought the old couple wouldn't enjoy their fortune. He told his wife: 'Grain fills the granary, beans fill the granary, why bother working hard in the fields?'

[P10] "No-bottom Pot" thought life was going well and had no worries. She told her husband: "We have summer clothes, we have cotton quilts, weaving cloth is not as good as sleeping." 
Neither of them took the elders' words to heart. Every day, they did nothing but eat, drink, and play, and still ate, drank, and played. Living off their savings, in just a few years, the fields became overgrown, and there was no grain left at home.

[P11] On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, the north wind howled, and snowflakes drifted down, as big as palms.
"Sleepyhead" and "Bottomless Pot" had nothing to eat or wear, huddled in their broken house, shivering.
"Shivering, shivering, I miss Mom's steamed white buns so much." "Oh dear, oh dear, I'll sweep up some mixed grains to make a bowl of porridge." The grains were collected from the bottom of jars, cracks in the grain storage, walls, and even mouse holes...好不容易找出来的。谁知他们端起碗刚想喝，一阵大风刮来，房子“呼啦”一下塌了。
They had barely lifted the bowl to drink when a strong wind blew, and the house collapsed with a "whoosh!"

[P12] According to this legend, every year on Laba, every household boils a pot of mixed grain porridge, drinks it to celebrate the festival, and uses it to remind themselves to cherish their lives.

The old saying goes, 'Laba porridge brings news.' Laba porridge is the most important food on Laba Festival. Don't underestimate this porridge—how it's made and what ingredients are used are all very particular.

During the Ming Dynasty, the emperor's Laba porridge was made like this: a few days before Laba, red dates were crushed and soaked in water. On the morning of Laba, glutinous rice, white fruit, walnut kernels, chestnuts, and water chestnut were added to cook the porridge. Although common people didn't have such elaborate preparations, they still added many ingredients. In the Qing Dynasty, common people used yellow rice, white rice, glutinous rice, millet, water chestnut rice, chestnuts, red kidney beans, and peeled date paste, all cooked together in water. Then, dyed red peach kernels, apricot kernels, melon seeds, peanuts, hazelnuts, pine nuts, as well as white sugar, brown sugar, and grapes were added, making it both beautiful and delicious.

Each of these ingredients has symbolic meaning: longan symbolizes wealth and reunion, lily symbolizes harmony in all matters, red dates and peanuts symbolize having children early, lotus seeds symbolize enduring love, walnuts symbolize happiness and harmony, dried tangerine peel and chestnuts symbolize great luck and prosperity. Everyone hopes for a better life in the future.

[P13] Besides Laba porridge, in northern China, people also make Laba garlic on Laba Day, which is enjoyed during the Spring Festival. The method for making Laba garlic is very simple: on Laba Day, put peeled garlic cloves into a jar filled with vinegar, seal it, and then place it in a cool spot. After being soaked in vinegar, the garlic becomes much milder in spiciness and tastes tender and crisp. The vinegar, now infused with garlic flavor, is called 'Laba vinegar'. The garlic not only changes in taste but also in color—it turns greener over time. When done well, the entire garlic clove becomes a vibrant green, looking like jade. The main way to tell if Laba garlic is successful is by checking if it has turned green. This garlic can help keep you warm and even prevent colds.
Of course, Laba garlic is mainly prepared for the dumplings eaten on New Year's Eve. If you start soaking it on Laba Day, it will be ready by New Year's Day. Nowadays, with heating, Laba garlic can be ready in just a few days, or even a few days later, and it's still called Laba garlic. On New Year's Eve, eating hot, steaming dumplings with a bite of Laba garlic is simply delicious!

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《腊八节的故事》的封面，画面中一位女子正扶起另一位倒地的女子，背景为暖色调，下方标注出版社为连环画出版社。
[P2] 本页为绘本《腊八节的故事》的扉页，左侧显示书名、改编者和绘画者信息，右侧为一幅雪景插画，描绘了被大雪覆盖的村庄和山峦。
[P3] 本页介绍了腊八节的由来和习俗，说明腊月初八人们要喝腊八粥，并详细描述了腊八粥的食材和制作过程。画面左侧为一位女子在灶台前准备腊八粥，右侧为摆满菜肴的餐桌。
[P4] 本页分为左右两部分：左侧描绘爷爷和孙女在餐桌前喝腊八粥，爷爷开始讲述故事；右侧画面切换到故事场景，展示一家三口在古代的日常劳作，为故事的展开做铺垫。
[P5] 本页通过左右两幅画面分别描绘了爸爸勤劳下地干活和妈妈节俭缝补衣物的场景，并配以文字说明他们各自的美德和口头禅，展现了家庭勤俭持家的氛围。
[P6] 本页通过左右两幅画面对比，左侧描绘了家庭富足的景象，右侧则引出其懒惰的儿子，邻居称他为“瞌睡虫”，为后续故事发展埋下伏笔。
[P7] 老两口年纪大了，分别对儿子劝诫，希望他学会种地、学会过日子，为将来做打算。
[P8] 本页通过左右两幅画面，描述了懒惰的‘瞌睡虫’娶了一个同样懒惰的媳妇，邻居称她为‘没底锅’，进一步刻画了这对懒惰夫妻的形象。
[P9] 本页讲述老两口病重时嘱咐懒惰的儿女要勤劳节俭，不久后去世；而儿子‘瞌睡虫’却认为有粮有豆无需劳作，继续懒惰享福。
[P10] 本页通过左右两幅画面，左侧描绘了懒惰的媳妇“没底锅”对丈夫说宁愿睡觉也不愿织布，右侧则展示这对夫妻因不听老人劝告、终日吃喝玩乐，导致家境败落，土地荒芜、粮食耗尽的后果。
[P11] 本页描绘了懒惰的夫妻“瞌睡虫”和“没底锅”在寒冬腊月因家境败落而饥寒交迫，最终房屋被大风刮塌的悲惨结局。
[P12] 本页通过图文结合的方式，介绍了腊八节的传统习俗和腊八粥的制作方法及象征意义，强调了珍惜生活、期盼美好未来的文化内涵。
[P13] 本页左侧介绍了北方腊八节泡腊八蒜的习俗、制作方法及食用价值；右侧则列出了“毛毛虫童书馆”系列丛书的书目，并附有图书的CIP数据信息。
